entries.title: Psalms 97:1
segments:
. The writer celebrates the Lord's dominion over nations and nature, describes its effect on foes and friends, and exhorts and encourages the latter. 
 
    1, 2. This dominion is a cause of joy, because, even though our minds are oppressed with terror before the throne of the King of kings (
), we know it is based on righteous principles and judgments which are according to truth.

segments:

    all ye gods--literally, "all ye angels" (
). Paul quotes, not as a prophecy, but as language used in regard to the Lord Jehovah, who in the Old Testament theophania is the second person of the Godhead.
